messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: Sev2 continuous-batcher (us-east-1) — sustained latency spike + CUDA OOMs detected. Alert rule: continuous-batcher.latency_p95 > 1200ms and container_restarts > 3. Runbook: /runbooks/continuous-batcher. Please acknowledge.

Alex Kim: acked — oncall here, joining. Seeing global error rate up ~1.8% and several pods restarting.

Priya Rao: any immediate customer symptoms? analytics shows a subset of high-throughput customers saw 5xx or timeouts. sending list to #customer-success.

Devon Chen: logs from cb-pod-7 show repeated failures: 
```
E CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 512MB; stack trace ...
W batcher: queue length growing from 0 -> 4000 in 2m
I deadlock: batch dispatch stuck waiting on token stream
```

Samir Patel: that looks like uncontrolled batch growth + KV cache pressure. Could be a regression in batching windowing. Priority: stop the growth, restore latency.

Alex Kim: mitigation plan: 1) scale down batcher pool to 2 pods; 2) reduce max_batch_size and max_batch_tokens; 3) route traffic to fallback smaller model for high-QPS customers. I'll run the kubectl steps.

Devon Chen: I'll grab the rollout flag to disable continuous prefix caching to reduce memory. Patch config: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS: "512"
  BATCHER_MAX_BATCH: "64"
  PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED: "false"
```
Applying now.

Maria Lopez: noted — notifying top 3 affected customers and offering status update. risk: degraded quality when on fallback model.

Alex Kim: rolling restart of continuous-batcher deployment in us-east-1: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher -n inference --context=us-east-1` (doing a staggered restart: cordon one node at a time).

incident-bot: Action logged: INF-2478 created for this incident. Pager duty: page engineers if regressions after mitigation.

Priya Rao: after patch and restart: p95 latency dropped from ~2200ms -> ~450ms, pod restarts reduced. However, one node flapped (gke-node-12) during restart — still investigating kernel OOM events.

Devon Chen: sample failing container stderr: 
```
2026-03-02T14:40:12Z ERROR model_runner: Caught exception in forward(): CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 1.2GB
2026-03-02T14:40:12Z INFO monitor: container exited with code 137
```

Samir Patel: node-level OOMs suggest memory overcommit by other pods or transient kernel reclaim. I've cordoned gke-node-12 and drained it. Will reprovision if flaps continue.

Alex Kim: temporary traffic policy: route 30% of traffic for high-QPS customers to fallback-distill-1 model in us-east-1 to reduce per-request memory demand. Config pushed to routing layer.

Priya Rao: customer impact update: ~12 customers experienced timeouts; only 3 had degraded responses due to fallback model. CS notified and offered rate credits where SLA hit.

Maria Lopez: logging ticket for CS follow-up with list of affected accounts attached to INF-2478.

Devon Chen: observed root cause hypothesis: batching window growth when a downstream queue starves the dispatcher thread; batches accumulate indefinitely until memory pressure causes CUDA OOM -> container exit -> node pressure -> flaps. Need to add guard rails.

Samir Patel: immediate permanent mitigations before postmortem: 
- enforce hard cap on batch size and max tokens (both at runtime and in config),
- watchdog to drop/dispatch oversized batches after 200ms,
- on-container start fail-fast if GPU memory below threshold,
- add circuit-breaker to routing so a single batcher can't take > X% of traffic.

Alex Kim: agreed. I'm opening a follow-up RFC for batching backpressure and adding a canary with smaller batch windows. Assigning owners: Devon for code fix (+test harness), Samir for infra/circuit-breaker, Priya for incident comms.

Priya Rao: handing off to Samir — I need to go offline in 20m. Samir, you're oncall owner. Please update pager if critical regressions. :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: taking over. Will monitor for 1 hour and then schedule postmortem run. tagging @devex for possible SDK changes.

incident-bot: Incident INF-2478 status: mitigated -> partial-service-restored. Root-cause unknown. Postmortem required. Severity annotated: Sev2 -> potential customer impact and multiple container/node restarts.

Alex Kim: notes to include in postmortem: timeline, config changes applied (BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS, BATCHER_MAX_BATCH, PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED false), nodes cordoned, fallback model routing, customers impacted, logs (OOM stack), and reproducer steps.

Maria Lopez: adding retrospective action items: improved alert thresholds to detect queue growth, runbook update for node cordon/drain during memory OOMs, and customer comms template.

Devon Chen: local repro on dev cluster reproduces batch growth when downstream ack stalls. I'll push a unit test that simulates starvation and assert dispatch after 200ms.

Samir Patel: leaving a note: if we see CUDA OOMs again after these mitigations, escalate to infra and consider node type with more GPU memory or stricter tenant isolation.

Alex Kim: thanks all. Closing active paging — will reopen if errors spike again. Postmortem draft target: 2026-03-05.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 2026-03-02T15:06Z. Reference INF-2478.
